**General**
- /
- /issues

- \<user\>

**Issue/Pull Screen**

title: Update build instructions in the documentation
body:
Hi! I was having issues on the latest release with singing in (just boots me back to the "Sign in with Github" screen), so I decided to try the latest version from git before looking into writing an issue about this. However, the branch does not appear to build on my machine. I followed the instructions at the end of the README, but one of the dependencies appears to have changed URL from `https://github.com/NamanShergill/gql` to `https://github.com/gql-dart/gql`. I was able to get `flutter pub get` to run without errors by also adding a line to force it to use a very old commit:

```
      ref: c4fc5c50e6c772b4264d2dd173c4bac1a940c8cf
```

However, subsequently running `flutter build apk` yielded a message about Java and Gradle incompatibilities, linking me [here](https://docs.flutter.dev/release/breaking-changes/android-java-gradle-migration-guide). I followed the instructions to update the Gradle version, and now I'm getting a bunch of build errors, so I think I'm definitely missing something:

[build_logs.txt](https://github.com/NamanShergill/diohub/files/12440967/build_logs.txt)

title: Preview Pictures Instead of URL
body:
whenever one taps on an image asset, they are currently given its URL.

there are two caveats with this.

first off, the field displaying this URL does not allow for text selection ; so there effectively is no native way to copy it.

secondly, it poses a UX issue, in that this is both unexpected and undesirable behaviour. upon clicking on such an asset, one expects for the ability to zoom into a fully width copy of it.

note that this last point not being true would have been *fine* as a workaround —had we had the ability to actually make use of said link to begin with.

title: Add organization profiles and organization repository support
body:
## Summary

DioHub could list the viewer's organizations, but tapping one failed: the profile query used GitHub's `user(login:)` field, which only resolves User accounts and returns `null` for organizations. Organization repos were therefore unreachable.

This adds end-to-end organization support after login:

- Profiles now resolve through `repositoryOwner(login:)`, with separate `User` and `Organization` fragments. Existing user behaviour is unchanged.
- Organization profiles have an **Overview** tab (description, members, repository visibility breakdown, verified/membership state, links, pinned repos), a **Repositories** tab scoped with the `org:` qualifier, and a **People** tab backed by `membersWithRole`.
- The home **Organizations** tab now shows names, descriptions, repository counts and verification badges, with an empty state.
- User profiles get a working **Organizations** tab.
- Organization actions (follow/following, contributions) are hidden; org-appropriate actions (Repositories, People, GitHub) are shown.
- Auth now requests `read:org` instead of `write:org` (least privilege; no org-write features exist). This makes it more likely that organization owners approve the OAuth app.
- Added a **Settings → GitHub Connection** card and an inline notice that link to GitHub's OAuth app organization-access page, since GitHub blocks third-party app access to orgs by default and there is no API to request approval from inside the app.

## Verification

- Regenerated Ferry GraphQL types with `build_runner`.
- Validated the new queries directly against GitHub's GraphQL API for both a user and an organization (including `membersWithRole`, `viewer.organizations` and `user.organizations`).
- `flutter analyze` reports no new errors or warnings in the changed files. The `development` branch already has unrelated analyzer errors from the in-progress model migration (e.g. `notifications_model.dart` missing, `flutter_dynamic_tabs` API mismatch), which are untouched here.

## Notes

The PR is from `AlgoQ:feat/organization-support` against `development`.
